title: Characterization of Metabolic Patterns in Mouse Oocytes during Meiotic Maturation
prior_qualification_check: Common-review contained a complete abstract reading but no linked source-specific primary appraisal; exact-ID/title search found no prior primary qualification.

read_depth.main_prose: Complete Summary, Introduction, Results, Discussion and experimental/statistical Methods
read_depth.key_resources: Relevant chemical, medium and antibody entries read; not the full resource table/bibliography
read_depth.supplement: Not recovered. PDF/XLSX requests returned browser-check HTML; Europe PMC supplement API returned non-OA error. S5–S8/S10/S12/S13 findings are read in maintext descriptions only.
read_depth.reading_credit_limit: This maintext qualification is supplement-limited; no complete-supplement claim or automatic outer-corpus/new-drug-appraisal credit.

model.oocyte_source: 3-week-old females after gonadotropin stimulation; denuded oocytes
model.intervention_setting: Isolated GV oocytes cultured in M16; selected matured knockdown oocytes underwent IVF and early embryo culture.
scope_limits: Meiosis and maternal oocyte-to-embryo transition, not somatic MVA cells
Hormone-stimulated oocytes may not represent natural ovulation
Steady-state abundance and enzyme protein levels, not direct metabolic flux
No live birth, mating/litter, offspring health or clinical fertility outcome shown

interventions.identity: Named metabolite; Sigma-Aldrich A3611 in Key Resources

exposure.timing: Main Figure2: GVBD at3h, MI/spindle at7h, polar-body extrusion at12h. Figure2P: 300 µM at7h.
exposure.formulation_limit: PUFA solvent/carrier and free concentration are not specified in read Methods; 0.1% DMSO control is explicitly described for inhibitors, not explicitly assigned to PUFA groups.

interventions.functional_results: 300–400 µM reduces first polar-body extrusion and increases spindle/chromosome defects; maintext reports little GVBD effect, data not shown.
interventions.positive_reversal: Washout restores much of polar-body extrusion; residual comparison to control p=0.063 does not prove equivalence or later developmental competence.
interventions.mechanism: At7h ARA-treated oocytes show lower NKAP (~70%) and BTG4 (~80%); maternal RNA deadenylation/decay is disrupted. NKAP cRNA overexpression partially rescues ARA-associated spindle/maturation defects.
interventions.mechanistic_exposure_limit: Exact ARA concentration for every Figure3 proteomic/rescue experiment is not explicitly given in the read maintext/legend; do not automatically assign the Figure2P 300 µM dose to all of them.

interventions.identity: Docosahexaenoic acid (Sigma D2534); eicosapentaenoic acid (Aladdin E100927)
interventions.maintext_result: Similar disruption of oocyte maturation reported (S6/S7).
interventions.assessment_depth: Maintext report only; supplement panels unavailable. No independently qualified dose-response or fidelity estimate.

interventions.type: Chemical inhibitor experiments interpreted as Δ6/Δ5-desaturase inhibition
interventions.maintext_result: No apparent effect on GVBD or polar-body emission (S5).
interventions.limits: Supplement unavailable; no equivalence claim. Authors acknowledge imperfect inhibitor specificity and possible sufficient pre-existing PUFA stores.

interventions.identity: Paper labels INDO (Selleck S5010) and BWA4C (Sigma B7559)
interventions.maintext_result: Dose-dependent reduction in meiotic maturation, larger for INDO (S5).
interventions.limits: Supplement panels unavailable. Enzyme specificity and eicosanoid-autocrine mechanism remain interpretive; not evidence that supplementing PUFAs improves maturation.

interventions.type: Endogenous metabolite measurements and SGOC-network components, not a demonstrated supplementation intervention
interventions.actual_perturbation: Shmt2 siRNA knockdown, with siRNA-resistant Shmt2 mRNA rescue reported in S13.
interventions.results: Lower SHMT2 and SAM, higher serine:glycine ratio, modest later maturation deficit, and markedly impaired on-time IVF 2-cell cleavage; lower DNA methylation and maternal-pronuclear H3K4me3.
interventions.maturation_figure_text_issue: Main text says no significant effect on execution of maturation, but Figure5E reports lower Pb1 extrusion at10h p=0.007,12h p=0.012 and14h p=0.008;8h p=0.600. Preserve the modest significant later deficit.
interventions.epigenetic_null: Paternal-pronuclear H3K4me3 p=0.735; maternal decrease p=0.006, n=15 zygotes/group.
interventions.causal_limit: Authors acknowledge methylation loss could reflect lower cell fitness. No serine/glycine/SAM supplementation rescue or methylation-mediated causation test is demonstrated.

interventions.type: Genetic PPP perturbation, not metabolite/antioxidant treatment
interventions.maintext_result: Slightly reduced maturation, excess ROS, impaired IVF-to-2-cell transition; siRNA-resistant mRNA rescue supports target specificity.
interventions.assessment_depth: Maintext report of S12/S13, native supplement uninspected.
interventions.transfer_limit: Does not establish benefit from niacin, NAD-related supplements, glycine, NAC, or another antioxidant.

bub1b_assignment.explicit_endpoint: BubR1 kinetochore immunofluorescence/retention in metaphase-I oocytes after Nkap siRNA (S8J/K)
bub1b_assignment.identity: Anti-BubR1 Abcam ab28193; kinetochores marked with CREST
bub1b_assignment.direction: Higher kinetochore BubR1 signal in siNkap oocytes
bub1b_assignment.interpretation: Checkpoint activation/retention with kinetochore–microtubule misattachments and maturation arrest. It is not total-protein restoration or beneficial checkpoint correction.
bub1b_assignment.compound_assignment: Not directly measured as a beneficial ARA/DHA/EPA/serine/glycine treatment effect. ARA lowers NKAP and its structural phenotypes are partially rescued by NKAP overexpression; that chain does not transfer the genetic BubR1 endpoint to a compound.
bub1b_assignment.fidelity_boundary: Spindle structure, chromosome alignment and K–MT attachment phenotypes are functional/mechanistic endpoints; no demonstrated restoration of chromosome counts, euploidy or functional MVA phenotype.
bub1b_assignment.supplement_limit: S8 endpoint and significance are author-reported in fully read maintext; native S8 images/quantification and proteomic TableS2/S3 rows not independently checked.

controls_and_replication.chemical_controls: Control medium for PUFA figures; 0.1% DMSO explicitly for inhibitors.
controls_and_replication.genetic_controls: General negative-control siRNA and siRNA-resistant cRNA rescue; exact supplementary rescue groups not independently viewed.
controls_and_replication.ARA_figures: Figure2 caption states three independent experiments and at least100 oocytes/group; Figure3 phenotype tests likewise. These are oocyte/experiment counts, not100 independent donor mice.
controls_and_replication.SHMT2_figures: Pb1 n=102 control/105 knockdown; IVF n=85/92; metabolite measurements300 oocytes/group; representative immunoblots use200 oocytes/lane.
controls_and_replication.statistics: Reported mean±SD; t tests and other specified tests. General Methods say experiments repeated three times and often representative data shown. No raw-data/statistical reproduction performed.
controls_and_replication.source_quality_issue: Figure5E numerical significance conflicts with the maintext's nonsignificant wording; figure-level result retained.

relevance_to_current_hypotheses.positive: Supports the importance of correctly timed endogenous metabolism and actual maturation/developmental endpoints beyond abundance markers; genetic rescue and ARA washout provide functional reversibility evidence.
relevance_to_current_hypotheses.boundary: Stage- and tissue-specific balance matters: excess ARA is disruptive here, so a broad PUFA-support hypothesis is not established. Increased kinetochore BUBR1 can mark ongoing attachment defects rather than improved function.
relevance_to_current_hypotheses.nominee_comparison: No niacin restoration, apitegromab compensation, or other current provisional nominee was tested. This source neither validates those hypotheses nor supplies a metabolite treatment competitor for MVA.
relevance_to_current_hypotheses.decision: Do not nominate ARA/DHA/EPA/glycine/serine/SAM from this paper as BUB1B/MVA rescue agents. Retain as mechanistic and adverse-exposure evidence.

remaining_primary_gaps: Native S5–S8/S12/S13 panels and exact DHA/EPA/inhibitor/washout/rescue exposures
Longer embryonic development, chromosome-number fidelity and fertility outcomes beyond the reported experiments
followup_decision: Abstract ambiguity is resolved at maintext level: PUFA challenge is adverse; SGOC/PPP functional rescue is genetic. Supplement-specific details remain explicitly unqualified. Stop at this bounded source; no broader citation chase or automatic therapeutic nomination.

integration.scope: Source reading declarations remain attributed to the delegated primary reader. Root performed the bounded checks below; no independent complete-paper review or biological validation.
root_checks: Figures2/5 independently inspected; dose-specific adverse/null direction and Figure5E statistics retained. No native supplement read by root.
